npcx: lpc: Remove WUI57 of table 0 initialization on eSPI mode Once ec receives LRESET/PLTRST on eSPI mode, both WUI57 of table 0 and WUI15 of table 2 will be issued at the same time. We don't need two WUI sources to indicate LRESET/PLTRST event on eSPI mode. This CL removes initialization of LRESET/PLTRST of WUI57 of table 0 in lpc_init() for eSPI. st-touch: Retry reading current firmware version Reading the current touchpad firmware version is failing on multiple Eve boards, resulting in non-functional touch after FW update. This change retries the command that reads the current firmware version up to 10 times with a 1 second delay between tries. IMO it is better to delay the boot than to potentially boot without a good touchpad firmware. BUG=b:35774858 TEST=tested on two units that were unable to update their touchpad firmware at boot and ensured that they did after this change. Change-Id: If57922cb80623323d51ab000779e45b6bd50df0d Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/449067 Reviewed-by: Charlie Mooney <charliemooney@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org>

Update TTS Engine extension to use an event page. This CL updates the TTS Engine extension to: 1. Use an event page, allowing ChromeOS to tear it down when it is not actively in-use. Chrome will also avoid loading the extension at startup, until it is actually used, which allows the TTS controller to query the extension's manifest for the set of supported voices without causing the event page to be loaded. Chrome will only (re-)load the extension to dispatch onSpeak, or system-upgrade, events to it. 2. Tear down the Native Client subcomponent when idle, rather than just disconnecting the audio output stream. Active NaCl plugins cause the event page to stay in-use, effectively creating a reference-cycle and preventing Chrome tearing them down when idle. This can save as much as 70MB of memory usage in long-running sessions, and helps avoid the TTS components running for users who aren't actually using TTS. BUG=chromium:616636 TEST=Open Task Manager. Load a web-site which queries TTS capabilities, e.g. https://www.guardian.co.uk. Observe that TTS extension does not load, or loads but then unloads again within a minute or so. Change-Id: I6d2d6d2f969ed2ad61fa7008b8b8e41093418f37 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/447000 Commit-Ready: James Weatherall <wez@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dominic Mazzoni <dmazzoni@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: David Tseng <dtseng@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ASoC: rt5514: Make hotword implementation compatible with Chrome Without this patch, the current hotword implementation works like this: 1. Userspace ensures no DMIC capture is active. 2. Userspace set kcontrol "DSP Voice Wake Up" to ON to load DSP fw and arm the DSP for hotword detection. The codec has to be in SND_SOC_BIAS_OFF, otherwise the kcontrol put is a no-op. 3. If a normal capture stream is started at this point, DSP is automatically turned off by codec driver, no auto re-arm. 4. DSP detects a hotword (IRQ is not wired up yet) 5. Userspace opens the hotword PCM device to read after a hotword is detected (needs IRQ notification). 6. Codec driver only sends 2sec of audio to the PCM device, then stops. 7. Userspace closes the hotword PCM device. This patch removes the kcontrol. Hotword detection starts when userspace opens the hotword PCM device. IRQ is wired up so that the hotword PCM device starts streaming when a hotword is detected. Normal capture and hotwording usecases are coordinated by the codec driver with mutex and a state machine. Normal capture has higher priority. Starting a normal capture while DSP is armed or streaming, pauses the DSP. When the normal capture stream is closed, DSP is auto re-armed. The hotword PCM device streams 2sec of audio first, following by zeros until it's closed. The new hotword implementation works like this: 1. Userspace can open/close the hotword PCM device anytime to indicate it wants hotword detection to start/stop. 2. Userspace can start normal capture anytime, though hotword will not be detected when normal capture is active. 3. Hotword detection is notified to userspace by the availability of samples from the hotword PCM device. BUG=b:35572001 TEST=sequences of normal capture and hotword detection Change-Id: I8bb5f5b4efb7324239ac72b25a2e7e640c8105ba Signed-off-by: Ben Zhang <benzh@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/444275 Commit-Ready: Chinyue Chen <chinyue@chromium.org> Tested-by: Chinyue Chen <chinyue@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>
